findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-interop-lrcat/src/catalog_bytes.rs:489-521 (seen set at :504 is per cell); src/extract.rs:504-518,598-604,635-639; src/source.rs:96-100
findings.evidence: No aggregate decoded or retained byte budget. The overflow visited set is local to one payload() call, so many leaf cells may share one overflow chain. Each Adobe_images row copies its text columns into PhotoProposal (global_id, file_format, color_label, capture_time, orientation); collection and keyword names are copied the same way. Only develop text has a retention budget (max_retained_opaque_bytes). Defaults allow 16M page reads x 64 KiB pages. About 62k rows x 16 MiB (max_payload) can be retained from an input under 1 GiB, which ends in OOM and an abort rather than a typed Limit. A legitimate file never shares overflow pages.
findings.remediation: Extraction-wide visited set for overflow pages (Cycle on reuse) plus an aggregate retained-text budget

findings.evidence: count() sets lost = seen.saturating_sub(mapped), so reconciles() (rows_seen == mapped + lost) is true by construction. Both test asserts of p.reconciles() check nothing. Per-entity loss-note counts are never compared with `lost`. Example: AgLibraryRootFolder/Folder/File call count(n, n), so a row whose text failed to decode is logged as a loss and still counted as mapped. The explicit tuple asserts at :458/:470/:479 are real, but they cover only develop and count-only tables.
findings.remediation: Derive `lost` from per-row loss events and assert seen == mapped + lost independently, or drop the claim

findings.evidence: layout reads Folio minimum_first_baseline_offset as an absolute offset from the frame top: first_baseline_pt = value, and value < inset_top is refused as InvalidGeometry. The IDML importer stores InDesign's MinimumFirstBaselineOffset in the same Folio field (proposal.rs:386), and InDesign measures that from the top inset. interop-layout reconciles the two only on a derived copy (value := inset_top + max(min, metric)), even for FixedHeight frames. Any other consumer that passes an IDML-derived Folio document to layout::reflow gets the baseline inset_top too high, or a refusal when min < inset. Folio's doc (folio layout.rs:147-148) does not state the reference edge, so the contract is ambiguous (STU-LAY-118 not re-read here).
findings.remediation: Fix the reference edge of minimum_first_baseline_offset in Folio docs/spec and make layout and interop-layout agree

findings.evidence: check_instances checks only that an instance property name exists among the component or set definitions with an equal type, and that bound variables are compatible. It never checks that a VARIANT value is one of set.variant_group_properties[name]. It also never checks that every VARIANT definition has a matching variant group, or that the instance's VARIANT selection agrees with its main member's variant_properties. Folio therefore accepts an instance with size='huge' that components later refuses as UnknownVariantValue (components instance_resolution.rs:343-347). Whether STU-DS-104/110 require this at record level was not re-read.

findings.evidence: scan_doctype classifies the document by the first '<!DOCTYPE' substring anywhere in the raw text (text.find) and does not skip comments, PIs or CDATA. Input `<!-- <!DOCTYPE x> --><!DOCTYPE svg [<!ENTITY e "...">]><svg ...>&e;</svg>` hits the commented copy first and finds '>' before any '[', so it returns ExternalIdOnly. That sets allow_dtd=true (:452-460), and roxmltree then parses the real internal subset and expands its entities. This bypasses the EntityDenied policy for internal subsets that R3 spot-checked as 'XXE refused'. External fetch remains impossible (entity_resolver None). Whether roxmltree bounds internal-entity text amplification is UNVERIFIED.
findings.remediation: Never set allow_dtd=true; or locate the DOCTYPE only in the XML prolog after skipping comments/PIs

findings.evidence: The DESCRIPTOR says save streams raw assets in chunks and handles 'zstd or shuffle_zstd assets one blob at a time', then concludes 'so save peak heap does not grow with asset size'. That is true only for raw entries. Session inherits the save codec from the source manifest (ShuffleZstd if any entry uses it, session.rs:569). The streaming writer buffers and encodes each codec blob whole in both passes, and verify_all decodes it whole. The package lane itself measured about 7 MiB of heap per 1 MiB shuffle_zstd blob, so peak grows with the largest codec asset. The session test save_peak_memory_does_not_grow_with_asset_size exercises raw assets only.
